hints: Look closely at the central linking group, the C=O joined to an O, to spot which homologous series compound R belongs to.
Split the ester at the single C-O bond, the 3-carbon chain on the oxygen side gives the alkyl part and the 1-carbon C=O side gives the acid part.
Think about which type of intermolecular force butanoic acid can make between its own molecules that an ester without an O-H group cannot.
walkthrough:
**Spot the ester group**

Great start, look for the functional group. Compound R contains $-C(=O)-O-$ in the middle, which is the ester linkage.

$$R-C(=O)-O-R'$$

**Name the ester correctly**

Esters are named alkyl alkanoate. The group attached to the oxygen is propyl, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-$, with 3 carbons.

The $C=O$ part including the carbonyl carbon is $\text{HCOO}-$, which comes from methanoic acid with only 1 carbon. So the name is propyl methanoate.

**Compare boiling points with butanoic acid**

Now think about forces. Butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, has an O-H group and forms strong hydrogen bonds between its molecules, even as dimers.

Compound R is an ester with no O-H group, so it cannot hydrogen bond to itself. It has only permanent dipole-dipole forces and van der Waals forces, which are weaker and need less energy to break. So its boiling point is lower than butanoic acid.

options.A: Incorrect on both parts. Methyl propanoate would be CH3CH2COO-CH3, with the 3-carbon chain on the C=O side, which is the reverse of the structure shown. Its boiling point would also not be higher than butanoic acid because esters cannot hydrogen bond to themselves.
options.B: The boiling point comparison is right, but the name is wrong. Methyl propanoate has the methyl group on the oxygen side and the propanoate (3-carbon) part on the carbonyl side. Here the 3-carbon chain is on the oxygen side, so it is a propyl ester, not a methyl ester.
options.C: The name propyl methanoate is correct, but the boiling point is the wrong way round. A common trap is to think more oxygens means stronger forces, but only butanoic acid has O-H hydrogen bond donors, so it has the higher boiling point, not the ester.
options.D: Correct on both parts. The structure is CH3CH2CH2-O-C(=O)-H, so propyl from the alcohol side plus methanoate from the 1-carbon acid side gives propyl methanoate. As an ester with no hydrogen bond donors, it has weaker intermolecular forces than butanoic acid, so its boiling point is lower.
